previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior amputations was admitted for worsening foot wounds on the right heel, lateral foot, and site of prior great toe amputation, with purulent drainage and foul odor. He had been unable to secure an outpatient vascular surgery appointment. Blood pressure was severely elevated on arrival, attributed to missed medications. Imaging showed soft tissue swelling without evidence of osteomyelitis. He was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral Bactrim. Vascular and podiatry teams recommended medical management with betadine dressings and outpatient vascular studies. His hypertension improved with reinitiation of home medications, and transplant function remained stable. He was discharged home with follow-up plans and instructions for wound care and medication adherence.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ was admitted on ___ for hydration prior to his 
procedure. Nephrology was consulted to aid on his management 
given his renal disease. On ___, he underwent balloon 
angioplasty of the right anterior tibial artery, first with a 2 
mm balloon and followed by a 2.5 mm balloon. Nine cc of 
visipaque were used and his right DP, which was previously 
absent, was palpable. For details on the procedure, please refer 
to operative report. After a short stay in the PACU, he was 
transferred to the floor. His vital signs, left groin, pulse 
exam and renal function were monitored. There were no signs of 
hematoma. Per Nephrology recommendation, his clorthalidone was 
held. His renal function remained stable, with creatinine of 1.4 
at discharge. 

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs. He was tolerating diet as above per 
oral, ambulating without assistance, voiding and pain was well 
controlled. He received a prescription for Clopidogrel for 30 
days. He received instructions on follow-up with Neprhology 
within a week and Vascular Surgery in a month. He was discharged 
home. The patient received discharge teaching and instruction on 
follow-up with understanding verbalized and agreement with the 
discharge plan.

Discharge Instructions:
Mr. ___, 

You were admitted to the ___ 
for management of your peripheral artery disease and associated 
non-healing ulcer of the right foot. You underwent balloon 
angioplasty of the right anterior tibial artery. The minimal 
necessary amount of contrast was used in order to protect your 
kidney function. The procedure went well. The Nephrology team 
participated in your care. Your renal function today is stable. 
You have recovered well and are ready to return home to continue 
your recovery. Please see the following instructions regarding 
your discharge. 

MEDICATIONS:
 Take clopidogrel 75 mg daily for one month.
 Take Aspirin 81mg (enteric coated) once daily. 
 Do not stop Aspirin unless your Vascular Surgeon instructs you 
to do so. 
 Hold Chlorthalidone until you see your Nephrologist next week. 
Continue all other medications you were taking before surgery.
 You make take acetaminophen for pain or discomfort

WHAT TO EXPECT AT HOME:
It is normal to have slight swelling of the legs:
 Elevate your leg above the level of your heart (use ___ 
pillows or a recliner) every ___ hours throughout the day and at 
night
 Avoid prolonged periods of standing or sitting without your 
legs elevated

ACTIVITIES:
 When you go home, you may walk and go up and down stairs
 You may shower (let the soapy water run over groin incision, 
rinse and pat dry)
 Your incision may be left uncovered, unless you have small 
amounts of drainage from the wound, then place a dry dressing or 
band aid over the area that is draining, as needed
 No heavy lifting, pushing or pulling (greater than 5 lbs) for 
1 week (to allow groin puncture to heal)
 After 1 week, you may resume sexual activity
 After 1 week, gradually increase your activities and distance 
walked as you can tolerate
 No driving until you are no longer taking pain medications

CALL THE OFFICE FOR: ___
 Numbness, coldness or pain in lower extremities 
 Temperature greater than 101.5F for 24 hours
 New or increased drainage from incision or white, yellow or 
green drainage from incisions
 Bleeding from groin puncture site

FOR SUDDEN, SEVERE BLEEDING OR SWELLING (Groin puncture site or 
incision)
 Lie down, keep leg straight and have someone apply firm 
pressure to area for 10 minutes. If bleeding stops, call 
vascular office. If bleeding does not stop, call ___ for 
transfer to closest Emergency Room. 

Good Luck!
